A tester played level 4 of *Bubble Farm*, a calm mobile game, and wrote six
notes.

| Note | Time | What the tester wrote | Criterion | Problem? |
|:---:|:---:|------------------------------------------------------|:-------------:|:--------:|

| 2 | 0:30 | Every bubble pop sounds exactly the same. | {{< answer-cell >}} | {{< answer-cell >}} |
| 3 | 0:45 | The master meter goes above 0 dB, and the sound cracks. | {{< answer-cell >}} | {{< answer-cell >}} |
| 4 | 1:00 | The storm warning is only a sound, with no icon. | {{< answer-cell >}} | {{< answer-cell >}} |
| 5 | | The level loads in 1 second on an old phone. | {{< answer-cell >}} | {{< answer-cell >}} |
| 6 | | The music and the effects have the same soft, happy style. | {{< answer-cell >}} | {{< answer-cell >}} |

## Task 1 · Evaluate

a) In the table, write the criterion of each note: clarity, balance,
consistency, repetition, technical, accessibility or performance.


b) Which notes show a problem (a score of 1)? Write "yes" in the last
column for each one.

c) Which note does the sound designer fix first: **A.** note 1, **B.** note
2 or **C.** note 6?

{{< answer-space lines=1 >}}

## Task 2 · Feedback

a) Which feedback for note 4 is useful? Choose A, B or C.

**A.** "The warning is not good." **B.** "I hear the storm warning at 1:00,
but nothing shows on the screen; it matters because a player without sound
misses the storm; try a flashing cloud icon with the sound." **C.** "Whoever
made this warning did a bad job."

{{< answer-space lines=1 >}}

b) Put the three parts of this feedback for note 2 in order: **(1)** "try
three takes and a small random pitch change" · **(2)** "it matters because
the player hears it hundreds of times" · **(3)** "I hear the same bubble pop
every time".
